Home.metaDescription: VLTone is a digital audio workstation for Windows and macOS: audio recording, MIDI, sampler, plugins, mixer and export. View the interface, read the manual and download available builds.
Home.title: Recording, MIDI, and mixing.
Home.copy: A DAW for Windows and macOS with audio recording, MIDI, plugins, mixing, export, and an AI assistant.
Home.overviewTitle:
One flow.
From idea to export.
Home.overviewCopy: VLTone brings recording, MIDI, arrangement, and mixing into one focused workspace. Start with an empty track and finish with a complete mix without breaking your creative flow.
Home.audienceCopy: Use your familiar VST, VST3, CLAP, and Audio Units on macOS. Export the full project or prepare separate tracks for the next stage.

what.question: What is VLTone?
what.answer: VLTone is music creation software for your computer, also called a DAW. It brings together audio recording, MIDI editing, arranging, mixing, effects, and export. An AI assistant helps you take actions directly in your project.

who.question: Who is it for?
who.answer: Musicians, vocalists, beatmakers, and producers. Use VLTone to record vocals, build a beat, write an instrumental piece, or mix a multitrack project. The guide walks you through the essentials.

beta.question: How do I join the open beta?
beta.answer: Register on the website, download an installer, install the application, and sign in with the same account. There is no additional application or invitation.

start.question: Do I need a separate account for the app?
start.answer: No. Sign in to VLTone with the same email and password you registered on the website. Your account page shows connected devices and your available AI quota.

platforms.question: Which systems does VLTone support?
platforms.answer: The main platforms are Windows and macOS. Each release page lists its available installers. Choose the file for your operating system and follow the instructions shown when downloading.

feedback.question: Where can I report an issue?
feedback.answer: Open Report a bug on the website and sign in. Describe what happened and how to reproduce it. Add screenshots if they help explain the issue.

Capabilities.metaTitle: VLTone capabilities — recording, MIDI, mixing, plugins, and AI
Capabilities.metaDescription: A complete overview of VLTone capabilities: audio recording and editing, MIDI, instruments, mixing, automation, plugins, AI, export, and project recovery.
Capabilities.title: Tools for
Capabilities.intro: Audio recording and editing, MIDI, instruments, mixing and export in one project.
Capabilities.statusCopy: We release updates regularly, fix issues, and refine workflows from musician feedback. The capabilities below work today, but the interface and individual details may evolve throughout the beta.
Capabilities.directoryTitle: From recording to the finished file.
Capabilities.directoryCopy: Each section explains what a capability is for, lists the tools available today, and links directly to the relevant chapter of the complete manual.

recording.title: Record and shape.
recording.lead: Vocals, instruments, and takes, right in the arrangement. Trim, stretch, and bring your best moments together.
recording.caption: Night Bloom: drums, instruments and audio transitions
points: Select an input, arm and monitor the required track, and record against the metronome and project tempo.
Layer multiple takes while keeping the source material available so you can build the strongest performance.
Import and preview samples, trim and move clips, and use Stretch, Loop, Vocal, Complex, or Resample modes.

midi.title: Notes, beats, ideas.
midi.lead: Draw melodies in the Piano Roll, build beats, or play a MIDI keyboard. Give your samples a voice of their own.
midi.caption: Warm Keys: chords and note velocity
points: Use the Piano Roll to create, select, move, and edit notes inside a MIDI clip.
Program rhythms in the Pattern editor and manage sound sources directly from each row.
Turn an audio file into a playable instrument with the built-in sampler while preserving its connection to project MIDI.

mixing.title: Every sound in place.
mixing.lead: Shape the balance, effects, and automation. Export a finished mix or individual stems.
mixing.caption: Night Bloom: channels, effects and shared sends
points: Channel strips include gain, inserts, sends, pan, fader, meters, mute, solo, record, and monitoring states.
Bus and Send tracks plus summing folders support group and parallel processing without duplicating identical chains.
Automate volume, pan, and plugin parameters, then export a full mix or stems with format, sample rate, bit depth, and channel controls.

plugins.title: Plugins and effects.
plugins.lead: Your favorite instruments, external effects, and a built-in equalizer, together in your project.
plugins.caption: Choosing an effect for Warm Keys
points: Use CLAP, VST, and VST3 plugins; Audio Unit is also available on macOS.
Plugin Manager controls search paths, scanning, rescanning, and the blacklist for unstable modules.
Find and replace plugins from the channel strip, automate exposed parameters, and shape sound with the built-in VLTone Equalizer.

ai.title: An extra pair of hands.
ai.lead: Describe your task. Get help with tracks, MIDI, and processing, with actions you can undo.
ai.caption: AI assistant in the Night Bloom project
points: Chat can explain the project and perform available actions involving tracks, clips, MIDI, and processing.
Results and errors remain in the transcript, while completed operations stay visible in history and support Undo.
Choose a VLTone account model or configure an OpenAI-compatible connection; exhausting AI quota never blocks normal production tools.

recovery.title: Pick up where you left off.
recovery.lead: Edit history, portable projects, and recovery after an unexpected shutdown.
recovery.caption: Recovering the Night Bloom project
points: A project stores tracks, clips, MIDI, automation, routing, and plugin state, with structural edits participating in Undo.
The background recovery journal captures state regularly and offers restoration on the next launch after a failure.
An exported project collects its document and associated media into a portable structure for another computer.

Manual.searchHint: Search checks titles, steps, notes, and troubleshooting.

categories.label: Getting started
categories.summary: Launch, workspace layout, transport, and the basic rules for controlling a project.

chapters.title: First launch
chapters.intro: VLTone verifies your account, audio system, and available plugins before opening the main workspace.
chapters.preparation: Download the installer for your OS from Releases. Close any other VLTone instance. Connect your audio interface before launching.
steps: Install and launch VLTone. On Windows use Setup.exe; on macOS open the DMG and move the app into Applications. Follow the instructions shown next to the download.
Sign in with your website account email and password. If you do not have an account, register on the website first. Your nickname and email address are different fields.
Wait for loading and plugin scanning to finish. The startup window reports the current stage; the first launch after installing plugins may take longer.
Create an empty project. Open Settings → Audio and choose the driver and output device connected to your headphones or speakers.
Check the main output pair. For recording, enable the interface inputs; the input on each track is selected separately.
Start with a buffer of 256 or 512 samples. A smaller buffer reduces playing latency; a larger one helps with crackles or high load. Keep project and device sample rates consistent.
Drop a familiar audio file onto the timeline and press Space. Check the track and Master meters, then set a comfortable listening level.
Save the project to its own folder with File → Save As. Continue with “First project: from file to export”.
chapters.result: The main workspace is open and the audio engine is ready for playback and recording.
notes: Scanning runs out of process, so a faulty plugin should not close the application.

problems.problem: Meters move but there is no sound
problems.fix: Check the main output pair, OS device and physical interface output, then make sure Master is not muted.

problems.problem: Startup pauses on one plugin
problems.fix: Note its name in the startup window. Check Plugin Manager and Blacklist after launch. Rescan after updating or fixing the plugin.

figures.caption: The startup window reports the current loading stage and plugin scan progress.

chapters.title: Workspace
chapters.intro: The arrangement is central, tracks and Browser sit to the left, and Mixer opens below. Web, Notebook, and AI can open on the right; the context panel follows selection.
steps: Use track headers for selection, mute, solo, volume, pan, and record state.
Drag clips along the timeline; the vertical playhead shows playback position.
Toggle Mixer, Inspector, Context Panel, Browser, Web, Notebook, and AI from View.
Double-click a clip to open its matching audio, piano-roll, or pattern editor.
chapters.result: You know where to edit project structure, track sound, and the contents of a selected clip.
notes: Internal editors use the same project and the same undo history.
The context panel adapts to available width. If a secondary button is hidden, widen the window or narrow the browser.
Select a track, then a clip: the inspector and context panel follow the current selection.
Hide unused panels through View to gain space. Timeline zoom and track height are separate settings.
Closing an instrument window does not disable its sound; bypass and closing an editor are different actions.

figures.alt: Main workspace with tracks, clips, and Mixer
figures.caption: The main window combines transport, track headers, arrangement, context panel, and Mixer.

chapters.title: Transport, tempo, and cycle
chapters.intro: Transport controls project position, playback, recording, metronome, tempo, and the cycle range.
steps: Click the ruler to move the playhead, or press Return to go to the start.
Start playback with Play or Space.
Enter BPM; arrangement and MIDI grids update immediately.
Drag a ruler range and enable Cycle to repeat it.
Enable Metronome before recording when you need a count reference.
chapters.result: The project plays from the right position, at the right tempo, and repeats a cycle when needed.

problems.problem: Space types a character instead of starting playback.
problems.fix: Finish editing the text field; transport keys are deliberately left alone while typing.

figures.alt: Arrangement with an active cycle range
figures.caption: The cycle range is marked on the ruler; Cycle enables it without moving its boundaries.

notes: Time signature is separate from BPM. Set both before recording so the grid matches the phrase.
For comparisons, set a cycle slightly wider than the phrase so effect onsets and tails remain audible.
Returning to the start moves the playhead, not clips. If playback is silent, check that the playhead crosses actual material.

chapters.title: First project: from file to export
chapters.intro: A complete starter workflow: add audio, create a MIDI phrase and export a file.
chapters.preparation: Prepare one WAV file, connect headphones and verify audio using “First launch”.
steps: Create an empty project and save it to a dedicated folder with Save As.
Set BPM and time signature. For an existing loop, start with its original tempo.
Drop the WAV onto an empty timeline area. With snapping enabled, move its start to the first bar.
Press Space and check the track and Master levels, then stop playback.
Add a MIDI track, assign Sampler and load a sound. Double-click to create a MIDI clip, then double-click it to open it.
Draw a few notes and adjust their lengths. Set velocity and listen alongside the audio clip.
Open the mixer with X. Balance both tracks and add an Equalizer insert if needed.
Loop the phrase, listen to the boundaries and stop transport. Save the project.
Open Render / Export, choose master mix, WAV and the required range. Set the name and folder, then render.
Open the resulting WAV and check the start, ending and clipping. Keep the project for future edits.
chapters.result: You have a saved project and an audio file that plays without the DAW.

categories.label: Project and arrangement
categories.summary: Project saving, track types, folders, selection, and safe clip editing.

chapters.title: Create and save projects
chapters.intro: A project stores tracks, clips, MIDI, automation, routing, and plugin state. Every structural edit participates in undo.
steps: Choose File → New Project or New Project from Template.
Use Save As immediately and choose a permanent location.
Use Save as you work; save reusable layouts as a Template.
Open an existing session with File → Open Project or by handing its file to the app.
chapters.result: The session has a permanent path and can be safely recovered and reopened.
notes: Closing a changed session offers Save, Cancel, or an explicit discard.
Keep the project and media in a permanent folder. The project stores structure and settings; deleting source audio may break file references.
Use Save As with a new name before major changes. Undo supports the current session; a separate copy preserves an independent version.
After moving to another computer, check media, plugins and presets. An unavailable third-party plugin is not automatically replaced.

problems.problem: The project reports a missing audio file.
problems.fix: Locate the source in its new position; do not move project media by hand while the session is open.

chapters.title: Tracks and folders
chapters.intro: Audio, MIDI, Pattern, Bus, and Send tracks are available. Bus channels receive main outputs; Send channels receive parallel sends. Plain folders organise; summing folders also mix their children.
steps: Use Add Track or choose a type from Track.
Rename and colour the track.
Select multiple tracks with Shift or Ctrl/Cmd and move them into a new folder.
Use Folder for organisation or Summing Folder for shared level and processing.
Collapse folders when their children are not needed on screen.
chapters.result: Tracks are organised by purpose, and summing is used only where it is needed.

problems.problem: Controls disappear on a deeply nested track.
problems.fix: Widen the track header area or reduce nesting; the most important controls remain when space is tight.

figures.caption: Folders show hierarchy, while multi-selection packs tracks with one command.

notes: Audio plays audio clips; MIDI sends notes to an instrument; Pattern combines rhythm sources; Automation controls a parameter.
A normal folder groups tracks visually. A Summing Folder also combines their audio; check child-channel outputs.
Open the icon picker in the track header. Add custom images through theme settings; color and name remain separate controls.

chapters.title: Edit clips
chapters.intro: Pointer, Knife, Eraser, Region, Mute, and Draw cover core arrangement edits; the context panel exposes exact values.
steps: Use Pointer to move, resize, and select.
Knife splits, Eraser removes, and Mute temporarily disables a clip.
Region selects a time span for deletion or repeat.
Copy, paste, repeat, and duplicate with Edit commands.
Adjust gain, fade, pitch, colour, and other available values in the context panel.
chapters.result: The arrangement changes non-destructively and every operation can be undone or redone.
notes: Shift extends a range; Ctrl/Cmd toggles individual items.
Moving changes a clip’s position; trimming an edge changes its visible range. Use stretching to change speed, rather than ordinary trimming.
Check the entire selection before bulk operations. Undo restores the last completed action; Redo repeats an undone action.
Zoom in and adjust a short fade to soften a boundary. Listen to the transition with adjacent clips.

figures.caption: The context panel exposes only the controls relevant to the selected object type.

chapters.title: Adaptive grid and context panel
chapters.intro: Zoom determines grid detail, while the selection determines the available tools.
steps: Select Adaptive for the grid and zoom out to see larger arrangement sections.
At overview scales the grid groups whole bars: 2, 4, 8 and onward. Snapping follows visible lines; zooming in restores smaller divisions.
Choose a fixed division for a constant step, or Off to disable snapping.
Select a clip for clip tools or a track for channel settings. Widen the window or narrow the browser to reveal additional controls.
chapters.result: Arrangement structure remains readable and snapping matches the chosen scale.
notes: When space is limited, the context panel hides secondary controls while retaining primary actions and values. Controls return when space becomes available.
The panel follows selected clips; track, note and recording contexts return it to the middle of the available area.
Zoom into the edit before working precisely: adaptive snapping depends on the visible scale.
Disabling Snap allows free positioning but does not move existing clips. Check the Piano Roll grid separately for MIDI.

chapters.title: Notebook and timed text
chapters.intro: Notebook keeps notes and lets you attach text lines to playback positions.
steps: Open Notebook and select Notes for text, headings, lists and images.
Use the formatting toolbar; additional actions are in the extra tools menu.
Switch to Text by time, enter a line and capture it at the current playhead position.
Edit text or timing in the table and enable text display during playback.
Open the notebook in a separate window if needed. Check the save indicator before closing.
chapters.result: Notes and timed lines remain available while working on the composition.
notes: Use the dedicated button to pause an animated notebook background. The gear button opens notebook settings.
Use ordinary notes for tasks and structure, and timed text for lines that should appear at a particular position.
Check timestamps by playing from the phrase start. Reordering text and changing its timestamp are different operations.
Save the project after editing the notebook. Before sharing it, check that embedded images are available.

figures.alt: VLTone Notebook with the timed text tab
figures.caption: The Timed text tab beside the arrangement.

chapters.title: Clip library
chapters.intro: Keep reusable audio and MIDI phrases in the project and bring them back to the timeline.
steps: Select a timeline clip and use its save-to-clip-library command.
Open the library and inspect the new card. Saving a copy does not delete the original clip.
Give the variant a useful name so it is easy to distinguish.
Find the card using search and drag it to the intended position on a compatible track.
Use the restore-to-original-position action when the initial placement is needed.
Save the project. Check focus before Delete: deleting a library card and an arrangement clip are separate actions.
chapters.result: The phrase is available for reuse without finding and copying the original track clip.

categories.label: Audio and recording
categories.summary: File import, Browser, audio clip editing, recording, and take layers.

chapters.title: Import and browse files
chapters.intro: Import audio through File, drop it onto the arrangement, or find it in Browser and preview it first.
chapters.preparation: Use a supported audio format and make sure the file is locally accessible.
steps: Open Browser and add your samples folder.
Select a file to see its waveform and preview it.
Drag it onto an Audio track or empty space to make a new one.
Use File → Import Audio for a standard file dialog.
For a new project from a template, configure Settings → Quick Import, then use File → Quick Import Audio… or drop an audio file on the VLTone icon.
Stop preview before comparing with the project if the signals overlap.
chapters.result: The file is an audio clip ready for movement, trimming, and processing.

problems.problem: The file does not appear in Browser.
problems.fix: Check the extension filter and folder permissions, then refresh it.

figures.alt: Sample Browser with a selected audio file and waveform
figures.caption: The preview strip lets you audition material before adding it.

figures.alt: Plugin category in the built-in Browser
figures.caption: Plugins have their own category and can be inserted without browsing file paths.

notes: MP3 uses the import decoder library; M4A/MP4A and MP4 audio use the native macOS or Windows decoder. Actual support depends on the file codec.
Lower preview level first. Browser preview level and track fader are separate controls.
Use browser collections for references to frequently used files; adding a reference does not move the source on disk.
Assign colors to folders; subfolders can inherit a color or use their own. This helps distinguish drums, vocals and effects.
After import, check the clip start and tempo. Choose an appropriate stretch mode if the file should follow project BPM.

chapters.title: Audio clip editor
chapters.intro: Double-click a regular audio clip to open a larger waveform editor for precise work on its contents and boundaries.
steps: Double-click an audio clip without take layers.
Zoom and navigate to find the attack or ending.
Adjust available boundaries, fades, and playback properties.
Close the editor; changes already belong to the main project and undo history.
chapters.result: The clip is prepared for arrangement without changing the source file on disk.
notes: Sampler looks similar, but edits an instrument rather than one audio clip instance.
Check that you are editing the intended clip; copies of one file can have different boundaries and processing.
Find the intended region first, then set its boundaries. Listen just before and after each boundary.
For local timing adjustments of individual attacks, open Warp Audio from the clip menu; ordinary Stretch changes the whole region’s duration.

figures.alt: Audio clip editor with a waveform
figures.caption: The clip editor offers a large waveform and precise controls.

chapters.title: Record audio
chapters.intro: Record Enable prepares the track and take options; Record starts capture from the current playhead position.
chapters.preparation: Choose an input in Settings → Audio, arm the Audio track, and enable monitoring when needed.
steps: Select the destination track and arm it.
Press Record Enable to expose mode, count-in, and monitoring.
Choose Layer to keep takes or Overwrite to replace material.
Position the playhead, enable Metronome, and press R.
Press Stop; the completed WAV appears on the track.
chapters.result: Recorded material is stored in the project and added to the selected track.

problems.problem: Transport moves but no input is recorded.
problems.fix: Check input channels, track arm, OS microphone permission, and the selected audio device.

figures.caption: Record Enable exposes take mode, count-in, and monitoring.

notes: Before Record, check the physical input and track meter. Microphone access may require OS permission.
If monitoring echoes or doubles, use one monitoring path: hardware monitoring on the interface or software monitoring in the DAW.
Make a short test recording to check level, input and clipping. A master fader cannot repair an overloaded input.
Enable Auto Strip Silence only after testing the threshold on similar material. Check quiet endings after recording.

chapters.title: Takes and take layers
chapters.intro: Layer Recording keeps repeated passes inside one layered clip without destroying earlier performances.
steps: Enable Layer Recording and define a cycle around the part.
Record several passes; each completed pass becomes a layer.
Select the layered clip and press E.
Choose the active take, duplicate it when needed, and collapse the layers.
chapters.result: Multiple performances remain in one clip while the chosen active layer plays.
notes: Take layers belong to one clip; duplicating a track makes an independent copy of the entire track.
Do not confuse the active take with the selected clip. Compare takes of the same region using the same playback range.
Save a separate project copy before deleting takes. Collapsing layers does not delete recorded audio.

figures.caption: Each pass remains a separate layer while the parent clip stays a single object.

chapters.title: Time stretching and tempo following
chapters.intro: The processing mode controls how a clip changes duration and pitch during editing and tempo changes.
steps: Select an audio clip and open its parameters or editor.
Choose Stretch for general and rhythmic material, Loop for repeating phrases, Vocal for voice, or Complex for polyphonic recordings.
Adjust Time and Pitch and listen at the working tempo.
Change the project BPM: modes other than Resample preserve clip start and length in beats while recalculating duration in seconds.
Check transitions, fades and take boundaries; use Undo to return to the previous state.
chapters.result: The audio clip follows the project musical timeline with the selected processing profile.
notes: Vocal compensates formants during pitch shifts. Extreme stretching and large pitch shifts require listening checks with your recording.
Resample follows a different speed-change model; automatic beat-position preservation applies to the other modes.
Resample links speed and pitch: slowing down lowers the sound. Pitch-preserving modes fit duration without that pitch change.
For large stretches, compare modes on a short loop. Rhythmic audio, vocals and dense mixes require different trade-offs.
Use Warp to move individual attacks independently; changing BPM does not replace local timing edits.

chapters.title: Precise clip parameter entry
chapters.intro: The inspector supports both parameter dragging and explicit numeric entry.
steps: Select an audio clip and find the numeric field in its inspector.
Drag the number upward to increase it or downward to decrease it; hold Shift for finer adjustment.
Double-click to type a value. With the keyboard, focus the field using Tab and press Enter or F2.
Press Enter to apply or Escape to cancel unfinished entry.
Scroll the inspector with the wheel or trackpad; scrolling over fields does not change the sound.
chapters.result: The parameter is set precisely; one completed drag or entry is one Undo step.
notes: Check field units: seconds, percentages, decibels and semitones control different things. Confirm typed values with Enter.
After Normalize, compare level and waveform. Undo restores both the setting and clip display.

chapters.title: Warp: audio timing with markers
chapters.intro: Warp changes timing within an audio clip using anchors. Use it to align attacks and rhythm without splitting every hit.
chapters.preparation: Select an ordinary local audio clip and save before extensive editing.
steps: Right-click the clip and choose Warp Audio. A bottom panel opens, bound to that clip.
Wait for transient analysis. Suggested marks do not move audio; click a suggestion to turn it into a marker.
Double-click to add a manual marker. Place anchors before and after the region to move.
Drag a marker to the intended beat. The readout shows source position, target position and movement. Alt temporarily bypasses Snap.
Ctrl-click or marquee-select multiple markers. Lock anchors through the context menu to preserve their positions.
Set algorithm, pitch preservation and transient sensitivity in the inspector. On narrow screens, its button opens an overlay.
Select a ruler range and use Suggest Alignment for assisted timing. Compare Before / After on the same passage.
Set Strength and tolerance. Manual and locked anchors are preserved; explicitly include uncertain attacks when needed.
For swing, choose a grid and Groove. Preview it; Save Groove stores timing from the chosen region for reuse.
Apply commits the proposal as one action. Cancel or Esc restores the confirmed map. Warp Off disables processing while keeping markers.
Ctrl+wheel zooms around the pointer; the wheel pans the panel. W shows Warp and X switches to Mixer.
Save after Apply. Rendering uses the committed map, so apply an unfinished preview first.
chapters.result: Attacks align to the selected grid or groove without overwriting the source audio.

chapters.title: Strip Silence: split at silence
chapters.intro: The command finds active regions and splits a clip at silence. Set the threshold for the material, not listening loudness.
steps: Select an audio clip and open Strip Silence from its menu.
Run analysis and inspect the highlighted active regions.
Set the threshold so useful audio stays inside the detected regions. Check quiet consonants and endings.
Adjust available pause and boundary timing settings. Compare dense and quiet sections.
Apply only after reviewing the preview. Listen to joins and add fades if needed.
Undo restores the original clip layout. Save settings for later recordings; Auto Strip Silence applies them after recording stops.
chapters.result: The timeline contains separate active regions and the source file is preserved.

categories.label: MIDI and instruments
categories.summary: Notes, piano roll, musical transforms, patterns, Sampler, and computer-keyboard input.

chapters.title: Piano roll
chapters.intro: Piano roll edits MIDI notes, velocity, pan, and controller lanes with the project grid, zoom, and cycle.
steps: Double-click an empty area of a MIDI track to create a clip without opening the editor. Double-click the clip itself to open Piano Roll.
Check the track and clip names at the top. The clip selector changes the edited phrase; in a pattern, make sure the intended instrument source is selected.
Choose Draw and click the grid. The row determines pitch and the horizontal position sets the start. Drag the right edge to change note length.
Pointer moves notes and selects a region. Eraser deletes and Knife splits. Shift-drag creates a copy of the selected notes.
Choose a grid division and enable Snap for rhythmic alignment. Snap to Scale constrains pitches to the selected scale; it is separate from time snapping.
Adjust velocity using the bars below the grid. The lower-lane selector exposes other MIDI controllers; check the lane name before drawing.
Use the top horizontal scrollbar and zoom controls on the right. Scrolling remains free during playback: Piano Roll does not pull the view back to the playhead.
Maximize expands the editor within the workspace to the right of the inspector and below the top context panel. Press it again to restore the previous size.
The Chords… button at the bottom or Alt+B opens the generator. Slide at the top or key 6 creates a control note; see the dedicated chapters.
Press Space to check the phrase. Closing the editor keeps edits in the project; save the project with Save.
chapters.result: The MIDI clip contains rhythmically and tonally prepared notes and controller data.

problems.problem: A note jumps to an unexpected pitch.
problems.fix: Check Snap to Scale and the selected root and scale.

figures.alt: Piano roll with selected MIDI notes and a lower lane
figures.caption: Selected notes share one context panel and can be edited as a group.

chapters.preparation: Create a MIDI or instrument track and assign an instrument. MIDI notes contain no audio by themselves.

chapters.title: Musical MIDI tools
chapters.intro: Tools apply quantise, humanise, legato, arpeggiate, chord, and other transforms with live preview.
steps: Select notes; without selection, a tool may use the entire clip.
Open Tools and choose a transform.
Adjust values and audition the preview.
Confirm the result or cancel the panel.
Use Undo if an already committed transform does not fit.
chapters.result: Notes are transformed in one undoable operation instead of being edited individually.
notes: Preview does not create another clip; confirmation records the final state in project history.
Quantize brings note starts toward the grid; strength controls how far they move. Test on a short phrase copy first.
Transpose changes pitches, Velocity changes note strength and Humanize adds variation. Change one setting at a time to hear its effect.
Generators operate on sounding notes. Slide controls do not become additional chord or arpeggio notes.

problems.problem: A tool appears to do nothing.
problems.fix: Check selection and values; some transforms are invisible on one short note.

chapters.title: Pattern tracks
chapters.intro: A Pattern combines several child instrument sources into one editable musical block.
steps: Create a Pattern Track and double-click it.
Add instrument sources or samples.
Rename, colour, reorder, and set level and pan.
Open a source piano roll to edit its notes.
Transpose or duplicate selected sources to make a variation.
chapters.result: A layered rhythmic or instrumental pattern is controlled as one group.

figures.alt: Pattern editor with several instrument sources
figures.caption: Pattern editor combines sources, miniature sequences, and core controls.

notes: Every source has Fill rhythm: once per bar or every 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 or 1/32 of a bar. Fill replaces source notes; the project meter defines bar length.

Drop one .mid/.midi file onto a source row to replace notes without replacing its instrument. MIDI file tracks merge into that source and project tempo is preserved. This import does not carry CC, pitch bend or aftertouch.
A longer MIDI phrase extends the clip and Pattern to whole bars. Undo restores notes and boundaries. Dropping audio onto a row replaces its sample; dropping between rows adds a source.
Other sources in the same Pattern automatically appear as ghost notes in Piano Roll. The Ghost Notes menu can hide individual sources or all of them.
Right-click the sound plate for the instrument, Piano Roll, Fill rhythm, sample replacement and other actions. Built-in Samplers also expose Cut Itself.
The editor represents a Pattern track: MIDI operations target the source’s first MIDI clip. If there is none, one is created at the first Pattern instance.
A step enables a hit at its position; loop the pattern and balance source levels before overall processing.
Fill rhythm fills a rhythm using the chosen settings. Check selected sources, density and length before applying.
Open a source’s Piano Roll for a more complex phrase. Dropping a sample on its grid replaces the sound only for a built-in Sampler.

chapters.title: Built-in Sampler
chapters.intro: Sampler loads a local audio file and turns it into an instrument for MIDI clips or the computer keyboard.
steps: Create a MIDI track, choose the built-in Sampler in its instrument slot and open its editor.
Load a local audio file. Check the waveform and Start / End boundaries, which define the played source region.
Set Root Note, the key that plays the sample without transposition. Adjust gain before adding effects.
Adjust the envelope: Attack softens the onset and Release sets the fade after note release. Very short values may expose a click in the source.
Enable Loop only when the source region should repeat. Without Loop, a short sample ends even if its MIDI note remains held.
In Resample, pitch follows playback speed. Stretch modes use time stretching; compare the result using your material.
Open a MIDI clip and draw a phrase. To replace the sound, drag a file from the browser onto the Piano Roll grid; sampler settings are retained.
In a pattern, open the Piano Roll of the specific source; replacement targets that source’s sampler. This replacement is unavailable for third-party MIDI instruments.
For pitch transitions, open Slide / Legato. Enable Legato for overlapping ordinary notes; drawn slide curves work separately and take priority.
Save the project and keep the source audio file accessible. Sample replacement supports Undo / Redo.
chapters.result: The sample plays as an instrument and follows project MIDI notes.

problems.problem: The sample plays at the wrong pitch.
problems.fix: Set the correct root note and check transposition.

figures.alt: Built-in Sampler editor with a waveform
figures.caption: Sampler shows the waveform and its instrumental playback controls.

notes: The waveform and file actions sit above the Playback, Envelope and Processing tabs. Instrument controls are grouped by purpose.
Drag controls to adjust parameters; wheel events over knobs and mode selectors do not change their values. The audio-clip editor shows only applicable controls.

chapters.title: Computer keyboard as MIDI
chapters.intro: Typing Keyboard maps physical keys to musical notes for testing an instrument without a MIDI controller.
steps: Select a MIDI track with a loaded instrument.
Enable Tools → Typing Keyboard.
Play the mapped keys and change octave or velocity.
Disable the mode before using normal one-key commands.
chapters.result: You can audition and record the instrument without an external MIDI keyboard.
notes: Conflicting single-key commands are temporarily released and restored when the mode is disabled.
If keys type text instead of notes, check focus; search, number fields or chat may be receiving input.
Check the selected track and instrument. Enabling the typing keyboard does not add an instrument automatically.

chapters.title: Slide notes and drawn pitch
chapters.intro: A slide is a control note: it changes the pitch of an existing voice without triggering another sound. One curve can contain several rises and falls.
chapters.preparation: A version 0.3.1 feature. Open a MIDI clip with a sufficiently long ordinary note. For a first test, use the built-in Sampler with a sustained or looped sample.
steps: Select the ordinary note to affect. It must be sounding when the slide begins.
Choose Slide in the top toolbar or press 6. One note / Chord chooses whether to affect one voice or a group.
Point at the grid to preview the link. Without a selection, the closest eligible note by pitch is used; a tie favors the later start.
Draw the slide and drag it to the required length. Its row sets the target pitch and its length sets transition time.
Double-click the slide to open its nonmodal editor. The initial pitch automatically follows the linked voice’s current pitch.
Add and drag nodes in point mode. Use Pencil to draw a rise, fall and another rise in one gesture. Alt-drag changes segment curvature.
Choose time and pitch snapping. Use numeric fields for precise node adjustments; 100 cents equal one semitone.
The shape menu offers Linear, Smooth, Wave and Return. Copy Shape and Paste Shape transfer the curve while adapting it to another slide’s duration.
Click Audition Phrase. The reached pitch holds after the slide. The next slide starts there; a later overlapping slide takes over from the earlier one.
If the base note ends before the slide, the inactive tail is hatched. Use Extend Base Note only when a longer sound is intended.
For a chord, select the sounding notes before creating a slide. The linked set is stored and every linked voice moves by the same interval.
Esc cancels the current gesture. One Undo reverses a completed gesture. If the base was deleted, restore it with Undo or use Rebind.
chapters.result: Pitch follows the drawn trajectory without retriggering the voice. The slide note itself is silent.
notes: The base note is not automatically extended. Its envelope release keeps the last reached pitch.
MIDI-file export does not include slide curves; use audio rendering to preserve their sound.
Slide editing can be disabled in older shared sessions; both client and server must support the newer protocol.

problems.problem: The slide is marked inactive
problems.fix: No eligible note is sounding at its start. Move the slide, explicitly extend its base or rebind it.

problems.problem: Drawing stops adding detail
problems.fix: A curve is limited to 256 points. Simplify tiny movements or divide the motion into consecutive slides.

figures.alt: Slide-note editor with several rises and falls
figures.caption: Nodes define pitch over time; the bottom controls copy the shape, manage links and audition the phrase.

chapters.title: Slides in plugins: MIDI, MPE and range
chapters.intro: Delivery depends on the specific instrument’s capabilities. The VST3 or CLAP format alone does not guarantee independent pitch for each voice.
chapters.preparation: A version 0.3.1 feature. Prepare a short test: a long note with a slide, followed by a chord.
steps: Open the instrument’s Slide Delivery control. Start with Auto and read the displayed capability status.
The built-in Sampler controls each voice independently. Additional MIDI-channel allocation is not required.
Use Per Note when individual-note pitch support is confirmed. If unavailable, choose a supported mode.
Use MPE for an MPE instrument and enable the same mode inside the plugin. Channel 1 is common; channels 2–16 carry voices.
Match the bend range; MPE defaults to ±48 semitones. DAW and instrument ranges must agree.
Choose Pitch Bend for a conventional MIDI instrument. It changes the whole channel’s pitch, including chords; the status explicitly indicates this.
If a Pitch Bend channel has conflicting slides, the later one wins. Use supported per-note expression or MPE for independent movements.
Check the curve’s extremes. Out-of-range sections are marked; reduce the interval or increase the range in both DAW and plugin.
MPE holds a channel through release. An unknown tail uses a reserve, defaulting to 2 seconds; set it for the instrument.
When all 15 member channels are occupied, a new voice is skipped and overload is indicated. Reduce polyphony or tail duration.
If the instrument supports no suitable mode, choose Off or another instrument. Audition after each mode change.
chapters.result: Slides use a supported delivery mode and the pitch range matches the instrument.

chapters.title: Sampler: Slide / Legato
chapters.intro: Legato automatically connects overlapping ordinary notes. A drawn slide defines its own motion independently of the Legato time control.
chapters.preparation: A version 0.3.1 feature. Open the built-in instrument Sampler and its Slide / Legato page.
steps: First leave Legato off and verify ordinary polyphonic playback. This is the default.
Enable Legato and draw two overlapping ordinary notes. The most recently pressed note has priority during overlap.
Set time from 0 to 2000 ms; the default is 100 ms. Switch to musical divisions for tempo-related transitions.
Compare linear and S-shaped transitions. S-shaped is the default and eases the rate at the start and end.
Release the newest note while the previous one is still held; the voice returns to the previous note. Check this on a keyboard or in a clip.
Switch smoothing from 0 to 20 ms softens value jumps during editing; the default is 2 ms. A continuous drawn curve adds no extra lag.
Incoming MIDI Pitch Bend defaults to ±2 semitones. It applies to the MIDI keyboard’s bend wheel; a drawn curve uses semitones directly.
For long transitions, check sample duration and Loop. Slide does not make a finished sample play indefinitely.
chapters.result: Overlapping ordinary notes connect using the chosen time and shape; explicit slides retain their own duration.

chapters.title: Chord Generator
chapters.intro: The generator creates a chord from scratch or builds chords on selected notes. Preview settings before applying.
chapters.preparation: Updated in version 0.3.1. Open Piano Roll and assign an instrument to audition the result.
steps: Click Chords… in the Piano Roll footer or press Alt+B. The command is also available in the editor’s musical tools menu.
In an empty clip, choose to create a new chord. Set the root and chord type to define its intervals.
Set the inversion. Enable bass doubling only if an additional lower note is wanted.
Set start position, duration and velocity to fit the phrase.
To harmonize an existing phrase, close the dialog, select the intended notes and reopen the generator. Check the selection-based mode.
Use preview. Compare chord types and inversions, listening to register and voice spacing.
Click Apply to write the result into the clip. Cancel closes the preview without committing.
Check the result in the grid. One Undo reverses the applied chord; unselected notes remain intact.
chapters.result: The chord appears at the specified position as ordinary editable MIDI notes.

figures.alt: Chord Generator settings in Piano Roll
figures.caption: Set root, type, inversion and length before applying the result.

chapters.title: MIDI recording and retrospective capture
chapters.intro: Record notes and controllers from a MIDI device, typing keyboard or onscreen keys. Recently played material can be recovered even without recording enabled.
chapters.preparation: Select a MIDI or instrument track and verify input and instrument sound.
steps: Select the intended track or arm several tracks. Check which tracks receive MIDI before starting.
Choose a mode: Overwrite replaces the recorded range; Layers keeps takes; MIDI overdub adds notes to existing material.
Set cycle and count-in if needed. Press Record and play; MIDI recording does not require an audio input.
Play notes, pedal and controllers during capture. Recording preserves performed timing without forced quantization.
Stop transport. The take is committed as one undoable edit. Open Piano Roll and inspect notes and controller lanes.
For MIDI Learn, open an instrument parameter’s menu, choose Assign MIDI Knob and move the desired control. Check that the parameter responds.
An assigned control records the instrument parameter lane. Check mappings after changing instruments; mappings are local settings.
If a useful phrase was played without recording, stop recording and count-in, place the playhead and right-click Record.
Choose Restore Played MIDI. New clips appear on the original tracks from the current playhead, preserving relative pauses.
Check and save the result. The buffer covers up to the last ten minutes, clears on project change and cannot recover an older session.
chapters.result: Notes and recorded parameters are saved in the project for normal editing, copying and undo.

categories.label: Mix and plugins
categories.summary: Channel strips, buses and sends, plugin insertion, format management, and parameter automation.

chapters.title: Mixer and channel strip
chapters.intro: Mixer represents tracks as strips with inserts, sends, pan, fader, meters, mute, solo, record, and monitoring.
steps: Open Mixer with X.
Set input gain and order inserts from top to bottom.
Use pan and fader for placement and level.
Watch the meter so peaks do not continually reach the top.
Detach Mixer from View when a separate window is useful.
chapters.result: Track balance is set, overloads are visible, and processing follows a clear order.
notes: The context control and mixer fader edit one value and stay synchronised.
Input determines where a signal comes from; output determines its destination. Instruments respond to MIDI, while audio tracks play clips or input.
Inserts process the signal in order from top to bottom. A send routes a copy to another channel with its own level.
Right-click a channel for automation, presets and timeline navigation. Master exposes its own parameters.
Use bypass to compare processing at matched loudness. Scrolling over a fader should not accidentally change the balance.

figures.alt: VLTone Mixer with plugins and level meters
figures.caption: Each strip combines plugins, sends, pan, fader, and track states.

chapters.title: Buses, sends, and summing
chapters.intro: Bus tracks receive main outputs for subgroup processing; Send tracks receive parallel sends, and a summing folder combines its children.
steps: Create a Send Track for shared reverb or delay.
Add a send from the source track and set its level.
Put the effect on the Send track and use a fully wet signal.
Use a Bus Track or Summing Folder for permanent subgroup processing.
Recheck solo and mute after changing routing.
chapters.result: Shared processing is reused and group level is controlled without duplicate plugins.

problems.problem: The effect is doubled or too loud.
problems.fix: Check direct output, send level, and dry/wet on the Send track.

notes: A POST send follows the source fader; a PRE send takes signal before it. Choose the intended behavior and test by moving the fader.
For external sidechain, open a compatible plugin’s menu and select source channels. Multiple sources are combined for its detector.
Avoid routes that feed a signal back into itself. If a connection is unavailable, check feedback paths and plugin restrictions.

chapters.title: Add and replace plugins
chapters.intro: Find plugins from a channel strip, context panel, or search menu. Formats are grouped and the search field keeps keyboard focus.
steps: Choose a track and an empty insert or instrument slot.
Type part of the name or vendor.
Put instruments in the instrument slot and processors in inserts.
Open the plugin editor for native parameters.
Use Replace or Remove; both changes participate in undo.
chapters.result: The plugin is loaded in the correct slot and processes the live track signal.

shortcuts.label: Find a plugin for the track

problems.problem: A plugin cannot be inserted as an instrument.
problems.fix: Check its type: an audio effect cannot be used as a MIDI track instrument.

figures.alt: Plugin picker with its search field
figures.caption: Search filters the list while retaining keyboard focus.

figures.alt: Inline plugin search in the context panel
figures.caption: Inline search expands directly over the selected track.

notes: Choose the correct slot first: placing a synth in an insert does not make it the track instrument. Use the processing chain for effects.
Save a preset before replacing a complex setup. You can close an editor without removing the plugin.
If an editor fails to open, check availability and compatibility in Plugin Manager. A plugin format alone does not guarantee every feature.

chapters.title: VLTone Equalizer
chapters.intro: VLTone Equalizer is the built-in 24-band parametric and dynamic EQ for corrective, creative, and mastering work, with Zero Latency, Analog Phase, and Linear Phase processing.
steps: Add VLTone Equalizer to an audio insert and open its editor.
Double-click the logarithmic graph to create a band. Drag to change frequency and gain, use the mouse wheel for Q, or enter values in the selected-band controls.
Choose the filter type, slope, and Stereo, Left, Right, Mid, or Side placement. Ctrl/Cmd-click selects several bands for grouped movement.
For Bell, Shelf, or Tilt, enable Dynamics and set range, threshold, attack, release, and the internal or external detector range.
Choose a phase mode. Linear Phase adds reported PDC latency; its Low, Medium, and High resolutions trade latency and CPU for frequency resolution.
Use A/B and Copy A/B to compare states, then save a user preset or choose one of the factory presets. Analyzer checkboxes show Pre, Post, and sidechain traces; Freeze holds the current frame.
chapters.result: The track is frequency-balanced with the required phase behaviour, channel placement, and optional level-dependent correction.
notes: If an external detector is selected without a connected sidechain, dynamics stays inactive and the editor shows SC missing.
All Pass bands remain saved but are temporarily inactive in Linear Phase mode.
Processing mode and Linear Phase resolution are intentionally not automatable because they change plugin latency.
Start with modest boosts or cuts and compare with bypass at matched level. Narrow and broad bands solve different problems.
Assign a sidechain source in the plugin menu before using an external detector. The Sidechain analyzer line helps verify the signal.

problems.problem: A dynamic band does not react.
problems.fix: Check that Dynamics is enabled, the range is non-zero, the detector crosses its threshold, and an external sidechain is connected when selected.

problems.problem: Playback shifts after changing phase mode.
problems.fix: Let the host rebuild plugin delay compensation; mode changes update the reported latency.

figures.alt: VLTone Equalizer editor with a vocal cleanup curve
figures.caption: The resizable editor combines the response graph, direct band controls, phase mode, presets, A/B, and analyzer options.

chapters.title: Plugin Manager
chapters.intro: Plugin Manager lists CLAP, VST, VST3, and Audio Unit, and controls scan paths, rescanning, and Blacklist.
steps: Open Settings → Plugin Manager.
On Plugins, verify format, vendor, and status.
Add only real plugin folders on Search Paths.
Run Scan; use Rescan All after major updates.
Remove a Blacklist entry only after fixing the plugin.
chapters.result: Available plugins are scanned and faulty ones remain isolated from startup.
notes: Do not add a disk root; it makes scanning much slower.
Do not add the whole system disk to Search Paths. Select installed plugin folders for supported formats.
After scanning, search by name and check status. If blacklisted, fix the cause before removing the entry and rescanning.
When moving a project, install the same plugins and sound libraries. Their licenses and content are supplied separately by their developers.

figures.caption: The main list shows recognised plugins and formats.
Search Paths limit the folders inspected by the scanner.
Faulty plugins stay isolated until an intentional rescan.

chapters.title: Automation
chapters.intro: Automation lanes move volume, pan, and plugin parameters over time; the curve editor supports precise point editing.
steps: Right-click a parameter and select Create Automation Clip. This works independently of the top toolbar mode.
To create clips by double-clicking, enable the automation button above the tracks or press Cmd+Shift+U on macOS / Ctrl+Shift+U on Windows.
Open the created clip, add points and choose segment shapes in the curve editor.
For an existing track, press A to show its automation lane and check the target: volume, pan or a plugin parameter.
Start playback and confirm that the parameter follows the curve.
chapters.result: The parameter changes reproducibly over time and is saved with the project.

problems.problem: The curve is visible but the parameter does not move.
problems.fix: Check target, automation clip enable state, and the required live plugin instance.

figures.alt: Automation lane below an audio track
figures.caption: The lane shows a curve on the shared project timeline.
Curve editor supports precise selection and point movement.

notes: With creation mode off, double-clicking resets ordinary knobs. Alt/Option no longer enables automation creation; inspector numeric fields instead open explicit entry.
Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A still deselects in Piano Roll. The automation mode shortcut can be reassigned in Keyboard Shortcuts.
Check the target before drawing: channel, plugin and parameter. Selecting another track does not retarget an existing curve.
Add nodes at key positions, then adjust segment curvature. Also check playback started from the middle of the curve.
For Master, open its mixer menu and create automation. A Master track appears on the timeline with child curves for volume, pan or master-plugin parameters.

chapters.title: Freeze and unfreeze tracks
chapters.intro: Freeze Track temporarily replaces source, instrument and insert processing with prepared audio.
steps: Right-click an independent audio, MIDI or instrument track and choose Freeze Track… .
Wait for preparation to complete; use Cancel if needed.
Continue adjusting the fader, pan, mono and outgoing sends, which remain live.
Choose Unfreeze Track to restore the original chain. Freeze and unfreeze support Undo.
Keep the project media together: the prepared WAV is needed to reopen the frozen track.
chapters.result: Audio processing load is reduced while original materials and plugins are retained.
notes: If the action is unavailable, check its menu explanation. Armed/monitored tracks, incoming routing, external sidechains, linked Pattern clips and external plugin-parameter automation can prevent freezing.
Editing source material or processing invalidates the frozen result. Missing frozen media falls back to the original chain.
Freeze saves DSP work; plugin instances remain in memory. Cloud publication uses original editable sources.
Freeze reduces processing load; Render creates an output file. A frozen track retains a relationship to its original chain.
Return to an editable state to change notes, slides or source plugins. Freeze the track again after editing.

chapters.title: Compressor and Delay
chapters.intro: Two built-in effects for dynamics and rhythmic repeats, added to a normal insert chain.
steps: Add Compressor to a track insert and loop a representative passage.
Choose Soft or Punch. Lower Threshold until the meter shows the intended gain reduction; Ratio controls the compression amount.
Attack sets reaction speed, Release sets recovery and Knee sets how compression engages. Change them one at a time and listen to the instrument onset.
Match level with Makeup or Auto Gain. Dry / Wet mixes original and compressed signals. Compare bypass at similar loudness.
Add Delay. Choose project-tempo sync, independent BPM or timing in milliseconds.
Set straight, triplet or dotted divisions. Stereo and Ping-Pong define repeat placement.
Feedback sets repeat persistence and Mix sets their share. Start with low Feedback and listen after the phrase ends.
Compare Clean, Telephone, Radio, FM, Tape, Drive and Lo-Fi. Low Cut / High Cut limit repeat frequencies and modulation varies their movement.
On a dedicated send channel, Delay is normally fully wet; the source track’s send controls the amount.
Include enough export tail so repeats do not stop at the final clip boundary.
chapters.result: Dynamics and repeats are configured with level and tail behavior checked.

figures.alt: Built-in Compressor with Soft and Punch modes
figures.caption: Threshold, ratio, attack, release and mix sit beside the response curve.

figures.alt: Built-in Delay with sync and filters
figures.caption: Repeat timing, stereo mode, feedback and character in one editor.

chapters.title: VLT Pitch: vocal tuning
chapters.intro: Built-in pitch correction for a single vocal melody. Chords, choirs and full mixes are outside its intended input.
chapters.preparation: Insert VLT Pitch in the vocal track’s Audio FX chain. Choose a short passage with stable notes for setup.
steps: Choose Key and Scale. For a custom scale, enable allowed pitch classes on the keyboard; the mode changes to Custom.
Check A4, which defaults to 440 Hz. Change the reference only if the recording uses a different tuning.
Start with Natural, Pop, Tight or Hard and adjust Retune Speed. Zero milliseconds is the fastest, hardest correction; longer times make transitions slower.
Adjust Humanize for sustained notes and Vibrato to retain periodic movement. Their influence decreases at very fast Retune settings.
In Settings choose voice range, correction amount and output level. Formants preserves the vocal spectral envelope and is enabled by default.
Compare Real-Time and HD. Stop playback and recording and disable monitoring before changing quality; a pending change applies when the engine is idle.
Enable track monitoring to hear correction while recording. The take remains dry; delay also depends on buffer size and other plugins.
Check input/target note and Shift in cents. If the target is wrong, first verify key, voice range and source material.
Send to All copies parameters to other VLT Pitch instances in one undoable action. Use it only when those voices should share the settings.
Save the preset and project. Freeze and export use the selected quality and do not automatically switch to HD.
chapters.result: Vocals are corrected toward allowed notes with the selected speed and natural movement.

chapters.title: Modulation Rack
chapters.intro: A serial chain of Chorus, Doubler, Flanger and Phaser with a shared Filter & EQ section.
steps: Add Modulation to a track insert. Start with one enabled module and switch the others off with their power buttons.
Adjust the selected card and listen to width, movement and level over a consistent loop.
Drag a card handle horizontally to reorder it. Clicking opens Move Left / Move Right; Alt + Left / Right also works.
Enable another module after checking the first. Order matters: each effect receives the output of the previous one.
Expand Filter & EQ. Adjust four bell bands, Low Cut and High Cut. Drag points for frequency/gain and use the wheel for Q.
Use numeric fields and keyboard controls for precision. Compare bypass without a large loudness change.
Save the preset and project. Standalone Chorus, Doubler, Flanger and Phaser are available when only one effect is needed.
chapters.result: Modules process the signal in the selected order and shared filters shape its spectrum.

categories.label: AI and Web
categories.summary: Model setup, safe assistant commands, audio generation, and the integrated browser.

chapters.title: Set up AI
chapters.intro: AI uses models supplied by your VLTone account or a custom OpenAI-compatible connection from Settings → AI.
steps: Open Settings → AI and refresh models.
Choose a managed model or add endpoint, model id, and key.
Add assistant instructions when needed.
Open AI and verify the selected model in its header.
chapters.result: The AI panel is ready to answer and execute available project commands.
notes: When AI quota is exhausted, editing, recording, plugins, and export remain available.
For a managed model, check account sign-in and quota. For a custom endpoint, verify that the provider supports the model.
Save settings and send a short test request. Read the error: access, quota, key and connection problems need different fixes.
Hide private keys when sharing settings screenshots. An external provider processes the requests and attachments sent to it.

problems.problem: The model does not appear.
problems.fix: Check endpoint, model id, key, and server availability, then refresh the panel.

chapters.title: Project AI assistant
chapters.intro: The assistant sees permitted session context and calls the same undoable commands exposed by the interface.
steps: Open AI from the View menu and choose Chat. The message field is available immediately; no starter option is required.
Check the selected model and access. If connection fails, open Settings → AI and verify the provider, endpoint and key.
Select the relevant clip or track if your request concerns specific material. Include its name and the desired result in your message.
Describe a clear action, such as “Create a MIDI track for bass” or “Explain how to set up a reverb send”. For a phrase, include length, tempo and key.
Drag a local attachment into the chat if needed. Check the attachment before sending.
Send the message and wait for the response. The transcript shows text and project actions; check which object changed.
Point to a message to access its actions. The copy icon copies text and the edit icon lets you revise the prompt; tooltips explain each button.
Audition the result. If it does not fit, use Undo or the available return-to-message action, then refine your request.
chapters.result: The assistant explains a task or changes the project through controlled command history.
notes: Stop a long request with Stop; completed operations remain visible and undoable.

figures.alt: AI Chat panel with a completed request and actions
figures.caption: Transcript separates answers, actions, errors, and run state.

chapters.title: Generate music
chapters.intro: Music mode creates an audio file from a description and adds it to a new Audio track.
steps: Switch AI to Music.
Describe genre, tempo, instruments, mood, and structure.
Start generation and wait for the result card.
Audition the clip; Insert Again adds another copy.
Rename and process the track like ordinary audio.
chapters.result: The generated WAV is saved and inserted as a normal undoable import.

problems.problem: The clip was not inserted.
problems.fix: Check the Generated folder and free space; the result card can insert it again.

figures.alt: AI Music mode with a completed generation
figures.caption: A finished result receives a card and appears on an Audio track.

notes: Generation depends on the selected service and allowance. If unavailable, check the model and account settings.
Specify whether vocals are needed, approximate duration and instruments. Check the actual tempo and file start before arranging.
Insert Again places another copy of the result; it is not a new generation request. Save after choosing a suitable result.

chapters.title: Integrated Web
chapters.intro: The Web panel opens sites beside the arrangement and can pass supported local audio files into the project.
steps: Open Web from View or the bottom button.
Navigate to an address or use page controls.
Drag a supported local audio file onto the project.
Undo the import when it is not useful.
Hide Web to return space to the arrangement.
chapters.result: A web source and the project are available in one workspace.

problems.problem: A page or video does not load.
problems.fix: Check connectivity and site restrictions; protected streams do not always expose a local file.

figures.alt: Integrated Web panel beside the arrangement
figures.caption: Web and AI are independent side workspaces.

notes: The browser uses system proxy settings and VPN routes. If a VPN exposes only a local proxy, enable its System proxy mode. Reload the tab after changing connectivity, or restart VLTone if needed.
After a network error, Reload retries the original address. Include the URL and error code when reporting a problem.
A webpage may need internet and its own sign-in. A VLTone account does not replace an external website account.
Use an available local file for import. A webpage URL is not necessarily an audio file URL.

chapters.title: Browser backgrounds and timeline video
chapters.intro: The browser start page and the timeline background have separate controls.
steps: Open Settings → Browser → Background collection → Browse background collection… and select a published image.
For your own start-page background, choose a local image, GIF or video in browser settings.
To use timeline video, open a page containing video in Web and click Use video as timeline background when it becomes available.
Choose a source if several videos are found. Use the speaker button for sound and Remove video background to clear it.
If a video is unavailable, open its source page and check that it plays in the browser.
chapters.result: The start page uses your chosen background and available web video can appear behind the timeline.
notes: The selected start-page background and cached catalog work offline. Removing an image from the server collection does not erase a previously selected local copy.
Start-page backgrounds do not restyle external websites. Video availability depends on the page, format and source restrictions.
Start-page background animation stops when reduced motion is enabled.
A background changes appearance, not the project’s audio tracks. Import an audio file separately for ordinary audio playback.
If load is high, disable the video background and compare project behavior. A saved link requires its source page to remain available.

categories.label: Export and settings
categories.summary: Final render, stems, recovery, every Settings page, and systematic troubleshooting.

chapters.title: Render and export
chapters.intro: Render / Export creates a final mix or separate stems with the selected format, sample rate, depth, and channels.
chapters.preparation: Save the project. Check the end of the arrangement and reverb/delay tails. Finish or cancel any uncommitted editing previews.
steps: Open File → Render / Export. The new window collects the main settings on one page; scroll its contents on smaller screens.
Choose the output folder and name. Check that the folder is writable and the disk has enough free space.
Choose a format. WAV is useful for further mixing; MP3 can be used for a smaller sharing file. Available options depend on the format.
Set sample rate, bit depth for PCM formats and channel count. Keep two channels for a normal stereo mix.
Set the range to the whole project or the intended section. Check start and end positions so the intro and ending are included.
Choose the master mix for a single finished file. Enable Stems and select the intended sources for separate track files.
Check the stem mode and processing: pre/post fader, Mute / Solo, plugins and routing. Read the summary and warnings at the bottom.
Set the required effect tail. Enable normalization or other processing only when needed, and compare output loudness with the project.
Add metadata and cover art if needed and supported by the format. These fields do not replace the output file name.
Click Render. If a name already exists, review the overwrite prompt. Keep the app open until completion; Cancel stops the operation.
Listen to the exported file at its start and end. For stems, check aligned starts, the file set and the required effect tails.
Audio rendering includes slide notes and committed Warp edits. MIDI-file export keeps ordinary notes but does not export drawn slide curves.
chapters.result: A finished audio file or a set of synchronised stems is available.

problems.problem: Export differs from playback.
problems.fix: Check master processing, channels, mute/solo, and external monitor gain.

figures.caption: Mix creates one file from the master output.
Stems save selected tracks as separate synchronised files.

chapters.title: Autosave and recovery
chapters.intro: A background journal records edits. After an unexpected exit, the app offers to restore a discovered session.
steps: Configure recovery in Settings → Recovery.
Launch the app after a failure.
Review the time and version of the discovered session.
Restore it and save immediately to a permanent location.
Decline only when the data is definitely no longer needed.
chapters.result: The last consistent project state is restored and can be saved normally.
notes: Recovery complements Save but does not replace backups.
Recovery does not replace Save. Use a permanent project folder and check the last save time.
After recovery, listen to recently edited sections and check file references. Save the recovered version under a separate name.

figures.alt: Project recovery dialog after a failure
figures.caption: The app presents a discovered session before opening the main workspace.

chapters.title: All application settings
chapters.intro: Settings groups controls under Application, Audio & Recording, Workspace, Appearance, and Account & AI.
steps: Application → General, Language, Keyboard Shortcuts, Recovery: startup project, display updates, locale, shortcuts, and recovery.
Audio & Recording → Audio, Recording, Transport: devices, buffer, take mode, metronome, and time display.
Workspace → Browser, Quick Import, Context Panel, Mixer, Notebook: files, fast import, tools, channel width, and notes.
Appearance → Themes, Theme Editor: ready-made themes, colours, and type.
Account & AI → Account, AI: session, access, quota, and model connections.
chapters.result: The application is configured for your hardware, language, and workflow.
notes: Some language and font changes require a restart; the page tells you when.
Change one group at a time and check the result immediately. Audio device settings affect sound; interface scaling affects display.
Find commands by name in Keyboard Shortcuts and check their bindings. Manual shortcuts refer to default bindings.
After changing theme, check grid and selection contrast. Mixer settings help fit channel width to the display.

figures.caption: General: startup project, refresh rate, and graphics quality.
Audio: device, sample rate, buffer, and channels.
Transport: playback, metronome, and time behaviour.
Recording: take mode, monitoring, and capture options.
Context Panel: tool visibility and behaviour.
Browser: preview, position, and import behaviour.
Quick Import: template, audio track, BPM and key detection.
Mixer: channel width and the default-size reset.
Notebook: background, visibility, and local fonts.
AI: managed models and custom connections.
Account: session status, access, and AI quota.
Language: built-in and imported locales.
Recovery: journal frequency and retention.
Themes: ready-made light and dark palettes.
Theme Editor: individual colours and custom font.
Keyboard Shortcuts: search, rebind, and reset.

chapters.title: Quick diagnostics
chapters.intro: Start with the narrowest subsystem: device, track, route, plugin, or file.
steps: No sound: check Audio device, master output, meters, mute/solo, and routing.
Clicks: raise buffer, stop background work, and verify sample rate.
Plugin fails: inspect format, path, and Blacklist.
Input does not record: check OS permission, input, arm, and monitoring.
Missing file: find the source before saving over the only project copy.
Still blocked: save under a new name and send a bug report with exact steps.
chapters.result: The issue is isolated while the project and source data remain safe.
notes: Do not delete recovery, Blacklist, or the project folder before making a copy.
If the wrong instrument plays, check the track, instrument slot and pattern source. Selecting a clip does not automatically change its instrument.
If an operation fails, reproduce it in a new project with one clip. This separates material problems from complex project routing.
In a report include app version, OS, audio driver, buffer, plugins and reproduction steps. Attach a short example and the expected result.

problems.problem: A window opened outside the screen.
problems.fix: Restart with the primary display connected; internal windows are clamped to the available screen.

chapters.title: Saved sign-in and offline access
chapters.intro: Ordinary application restarts restore the saved session without asking for your account password again.
steps: Sign in with an internet connection and allow the system credential vault to save the session.
On the next launch, wait for automatic session restoration.
If the vault is locked or macOS requires permission after replacing a build, click Restore saved sign-in and approve the system prompt.
After a temporary network failure, reconnect and retry the check; signing out is not required.
When the offline allowance expires, reconnect for an online access check.
chapters.result: The saved session is restored if it remains valid on the server.
notes: The 72-hour offline allowance is not a password expiration. An online check is required after it ends.
Explicit sign-out, session revocation or account suspension can require a new sign-in. Do not remove the saved session merely because of a temporary network failure.
Do not delete saved credentials for a brief network outage. Restore connectivity and retry first.
If sign-in still fails, check the system clock, credential-store access and account status on the website.

chapters.title: Bounce: combine into audio
chapters.intro: Bounce in Place turns selected material into an audio clip inside the project, useful for combined processing of several tracks.
chapters.preparation: Combining multiple sources is updated in 0.3.1. Check the selection and save the project before processing.
steps: Select the intended clips or tracks. Exclude anything that should remain separate.
Open Bounce in Place. With multiple source tracks, the result is a combined audio clip.
Set range and available processing options. Check the listed effects and sources.
Start processing and wait for completion. Cancellation should not leave an unfinished result.
Listen to the new clip with the project. Make sure original sources do not double it where they should be muted.
Check the region boundaries. One Undo reverses the operation; Redo restores the result.
chapters.result: The project contains one audio clip of the selected sources, ready for ordinary editing and processing.
